# High-Voltage (HV) and Medium-Voltage (MV) Power Distribution {#sec-hv-mv-power-distribution}

## Technical-Commercial Overview: Electrical Distribution Hierarchy {.unnumbered}

The electrical distribution system forms the single largest capital cost driver of a mission-critical data center, representing roughly **40% to 48% of total project CapEx** (@tbl-capex-distribution, with core MV/LV distribution packages alone accounting for 25%+) [@ref03_amanengineering; @ref37_aecom_meh2024]. Standard measurement frameworks—including **RICS NRM2 Section 39** and **CSI MasterFormat Division 26**—require granular takeoff across the voltage hierarchy shown in @fig-dc-electrical-hierarchy, from the high-voltage utility substation (@tbl-hv-mv-boq) down to white-space rack PDUs (@sec-lv-distribution-white-space-power) [@rics2021nrm2; @csi2020masterformat; @ref15_irecruit_qs].

::: {#fig-dc-electrical-hierarchy}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  U["Utility HV Grid Substation\n(110-220 kV GIS / AIS)"]
  MV["Customer MV Switchgear\n(11-33 kV VCB Line-Ups)"]
  GEN["DCC Standby Generators &\nMGPS Paralleling"]
  TX["MV / LV Transformers\n(Cast-Resin or Oil-Bunded)"]
  MLV["Main LV Switchboards\n(400-480 V Form 4b)"]
  UPS["Static UPS / DRUPS &\nLFP / VRLA Energy Storage"]
  BUS["Dual A/B Overhead Busways\n(800-5000 A) & Tap-Offs"]
  RACK["White-Space Rack PDUs\n(Dual-Corded IT Cabinets)"]
  U ==>|"Contestability\nDemarcation"| MV
  GEN ==> MV
  MV --> TX --> MLV --> UPS --> BUS --> RACK
```

## Utility interconnection substations: Gas-Insulated Switchgear (GIS) vs. Air-Insulated Switchgear (AIS), line bays, and transformer yards

Campus-scale data centers ($20\text{ MW to }200+\text{ MW}$) interconnect directly at high voltage ($110\text{ kV}, 132\text{ kV}, \text{or } 220\text{ kV}$) [@ref10_lvi_epc_manager; @ref11_irecruit_substation]:

- **Gas-Insulated Switchgear ([GIS]{.gls})**: Reduces substation footprint by up to $70\%$ compared to outdoor Air-Insulated Switchgear ([AIS]{.gls}) and encloses live buses against desert dust and coastal salt pollution [@sec_grid_code; @dewa_hv_regulations].
- **GCC Utility Demarcation ([SEC]{.gls} & [DEWA]{.gls})**: In Saudi Arabia (**SEC** $132\text{ kV}/33\text{ kV}$ or $13.8\text{ kV}$) and the UAE (**DEWA** $132/11\text{ kV}$), the MEP-QS must explicitly separate the **Contestability / Utility-Adopted Scope** (built to utility specification and handed over to SEC/DEWA ownership, including teleprotection, tariff metering panels, and fiber-optic pilot cables) from the **Customer Private MV Side** [@sec_grid_code; @dewa_hv_regulations].

## Medium-voltage switchgear assemblies: Vacuum circuit breakers, protection relays, arc flash mitigation barriers, and interlocking schemes

MV distribution line-ups ($11\text{ kV}, 13.8\text{ kV}, 22\text{ kV}, \text{or } 33\text{ kV}$, typically IEC 62271-200 metal-clad, LSC2B-PM, Internal Arc Classified IAC AFLR $31.5\text{–}50\text{ kA}$ for $1\text{ s}$) are measured per vertical panel cubicle (`No.`) [@rics2021nrm2; @ref10_lvi_epc_manager]. Critical BOQ inclusions frequently missed in preliminary estimates include:

1. **Sheet-Metal Arc-Flash Exhaust Ducts**: Custom overhead plenums venting hot arc gases from the top of the MV switchgear line-up safely outside the electrical room through blast dampers [@ref10_lvi_epc_manager].
2. **Kirk-Key / Castell Mechanical & Electrical Interlocks**: Preventing parallel closure of unsynchronized utility and generator sources across Tier III/IV distribution rings [@uptime2018tier; @ref10_lvi_epc_manager].
3. **IEC 61850 / GOOSE Fiber Networking**: Redundant fiber-optic patch cords linking multifunction protection relays (e.g., differential, directional overcurrent, arc-flash optical sensors) to the Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) [@ref14_cxplanner].

## Substation and unit transformers: Cast resin dry-type versus oil-immersed transformers, containment bunds, and deluge interfaces

- **Cast-Resin Dry-Type Transformers ($1.5\text{ MVA to }4.0\text{ MVA}$)**: Installed indoors within MV/LV skids or electrical rooms; eliminates oil fire hazards and bunding under NFPA 75 and SBC 801, but requires forced-air cooling fans (AN/AF) and room HVAC heat-load allowances for transformer no-load and load losses [@nfpa75; @sbc801_fire; @ref10_lvi_epc_manager].
- **Mineral-Oil or Ester-Filled Transformers**: Installed in outdoor yards; require reinforced concrete blast walls, $110\%$-capacity oil-containment bund pits with flame-trap gravel beds, oil-water separator drainage connections, and high-velocity water-spray deluge fire protection [@nfpa75; @ref10_lvi_epc_manager].

## Medium-voltage raceways and cabling: Armored MV cabling, trefoil/triplex configurations, cable cleats, and trench/tray routing

Single-core or three-core MV XLPE/EPR cables (e.g., $185\text{ mm}^2\text{ to }630\text{ mm}^2$ Cu/Al, LSZH outer sheath, AWA/SWA armor) are measured in linear meters (`m`) along the installed route [@rics2021nrm2]. When single-core MV cables are installed in **trefoil configuration** on heavy-duty ladder racks, the MEP-QS must measure short-circuit-rated **stainless steel trefoil cable cleats** spaced every $600\text{ to }900\text{ mm}$ (designed to withstand peak electromechanical fault forces at $31.5\text{–}50\text{ kA}$), heat-shrink or cold-shrink stress-cone termination kits (`No.`), and VLF (Very Low Frequency $0.1\text{ Hz}$) or partial-discharge site testing [@rics2021nrm2; @ref10_lvi_epc_manager].
